GABON Vice Mayor/CTFRB Chair Office of the Vice Mayor Catbalogan City, Samar Dear Vice Mayor Gabon: DILG Lega) Opinion No. 77 s. 2011 NOV Io This has reference to your 21 October 2011 requesting the Department's opinion as to the interpretation of DILG MC No. 2011-68 dated 09 May 20111 particularly the paragraph thereof which states as follows: "For safety reasons, no tricycles should operate on nationa/ highways utilized by 4 whee/ vehic/es greater than 4 tons and where norma/ speed exceed 40 kph. However, the SB/SP may provide exceptions if there is no alternative route. Please note that DILG MC Noa 2011-68 together with DILG MC No. 2007-01 was issued by the Department to regulate the operations of tricycles and pedicabs rendering transport services to the general public, pursuant to the DOTC's "Guidelines to Implement the Devolution of LTFRB/s Franchising Authority Over Tricyc/es-For-Hire to Loca/ Government Units Pursuant to the Loca/ Government Code (RA No. 7160). Under the Guidelines issued by the DOT C, as reiterated under DILG MC Nos. 2011-68 and 2007-01, tlFor safety reasons, no tricycles should operate on nationa/ highways utilized by 4 whee/ vehicles greater than 4 tons and where norma/ speed exceed 40 kph. However, the SB/SP may provide exceptions if there is no alternative route, Municipalities and cities are granted the power to regulate the operation of tricycles and grant franchises within their respective territorial jurisdictions subject to the guidelines prescribed by the DOTC pursuant to Sections 447 (3) (vi) and 458 (3) (vi) of the Local Government. In the case "LTO vs. City of Butuan, GR. 131512, January 20/ 2000/ the Supreme Court had the occasion to discuss the DOTC's (through the Land Transportation Franchising Regulatory Board) devolved power to grant franchises .to tricycles-for-hire to the LGUs pursuant to the above-cited provisions of the Local Government Code, viz : "The Depattrnent of Transpoåation and Communicationsg through the LTO and the LTFRB, has since been tasked with implementing laws peHaining to land transponation. x x x The LTFRB, upon the other hand) is the governing body tasked by EO No. 202, dated 19 June 1987, to regulate the operation of public utility or 'for hire" vehicles and to grant franchises or cenificates of public convenience Under the Local Government Code, ceHain functions of the DOTC were transferred to the LGUs, thusly: Sec. 458. Powers, Duties} Functions and Compensation. — xxx xxx xxx (3) Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code, enact ordinances granting franchises and authorizing the issuance of permits or licenses, upon such conditions and for such purposes intended to promote the general welfare of the inhabitants of the city and pursuant to this legislative authority shall: xxx xxx xxx (V!) Subject to the guidelines prescribed by the Department of Transponatjon and Communications, regulate the operation of tricycles and grant

franchises for the operation thereof within the territorial jurisdiction of the city, (Emphasis supplied), LGUs indubitably now have the power to regulate the operation of tricycles-for-hire and to grant franchises for the operation thereof, "To regulate" means to fix, establish, or control; to adjust by rule, method, or established mode; to direct by rule or restriction; or to subject to governing principles or laws. 12 A franchise is defined to be a special privilege to do cedain things conferred by government on an individual or corporation, and which does not belong to citizens generally of common right.l.a x x x .15 The devolution of the functions of the DOTC, performed by the LTFRB, to the LGUs, as so aptly observed by the Solicitor General, is aimed at curbing the alarming increase of accidents in national highways involving tricycles. It has been the perception that local governments are in good position to achieve the end desired by the law-making body because of their proximity to the situation that can enable them to address that serious concern better than the national government. It mav not be amiss to state, nevertheless, that under Ahicle 458 (a)13-Vll of the Local Government Codet the power of LGUs to requlate the operation of tricycles and to qrant franchises for the operation thereof is still subiect to the quidelines prescribed bv the DOTC. In compliance therewith, the Department of Transportation and Communications ("DOTC") issued "Guidelines to Implement the Devolution of LTFRBs Franchisinq Authority over Tricycles-For-Hire to Local Government units pursuant to the Local Government Code.' Pertinent provisions of the guidelines state: In lieu of the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) in the DOTC, the Sangguniang Bayan/Sangguniang Pang/ungsod (SB/SP) shall perform the following: (a) Issue, amend, revise, renew, suspend, or cancel MTOP and prescribe the appropriate terms and conditions therefor; xxx Operating Conditions: xxx xxx 1. For safety reasons, no tricycles should operate on national highways utilized by. 4 wheel vehicles qreater than 4 tons and where normal speed exceed 40 KPH. However, the SB/SP may provide exceptions if there is no alternative route. 2. Zones must be within the boundaries of the municipality/city, However, existing zones within more than one municipality/city shall be maintained, provided that operators sewing said zone shall secure MTOPs from each of the municipalities/cities having jurisdiction over the areas covered by the zone. 3. A common color for tricycles-for-hire operating in the same zone may be imposed Each unit shall be assigned and bear an identification number, aside from its LTO license plate number. 4. An operator wishing to stop service completely, or to suspend semce for more than one month, should report in writing such termination or suspension to the SB/SP which originally granted the MTOP prior thereto. Transfer to another zone may be permitted upon application. 5. The MTOP shall be valid for three (3) years, renewable for the same period. Transfer to another zone, change of ownership of unit or transfer of MTOP shall be construed as an amendment to an MTOP and shall require appropriate approval of the SB/SP. 6. Operators shall employ only drivers duly licensed by LTO for tricycles-for-hire. 7. No tricycle-for-hire shall be allowed to carry more passengers and/or goods than jt is designed for. 8. A tricycle-for-hire shall be allowed to operate like a taxi service, i.e., semce is rendered upon demand and without a fixed route within a zone.ß" Applying the foregoing premises to the complaint before the CTFRB, it is clear that the City has the authority to issue franchises to tricycles following the operating conditions set forth under the DOTC's Guidelines. Among the operating conditions reiterated in DILG MC Nos. 2007-01 and 2011-68 is the prohibition in the operation of tricycles along the national highways unless there is no alternative route as provided in an ordinance enacted by the LGUs' Sangguniang Panlalawigan/Sangguniang Panlungsod.

The wisdom in devolving tricycle regulation and franchising to LGUs is their close proximity to the situation which makes them in a good position in curbing accidents along the national highways. The DOTC's Guidelines prohibiting the operation of tricycles along the national highway as reiterated in DILG MC Nos. 2007-01 and 2011-68 clearly provides for an exception. It is therefore within the LGU's power to regulate the tricycles operation on national highway among other operating conditions as provided under the DOTC's Guidelines since it has a bird's eye view of the traffic situation within its territorial jurisdiction enabling it to come up with ordinances responsive to the general welfare of its inhabitants. The issue as to whether tricycles should be allowed to operate along the national highway of Catbalogan, Samar should not be confused with the issue on the franchises issued by the LTFRB to multicabs which are plying the same route as the tricycles since both the LTFRB and LGU's CT FRB have the authority to issue franchises, albeit on different types of vehicles. Notably, the Supreme Court, in the aforequoted case, remarked on the laxity of the grant of franchises to tricycles and it enumerated as well the applicable civil and criminal laws to be incurred by public officials in case of tolerance and negligence of their bounden duty to ensure public safety and convenience to commuters and pedestrians alike, viz: u The Court cannot end this decision without expressing its own serious concern over the seeming laxity in the grant of franchises for the operation of tricycles-for-hire and in allowing the indiscriminate use by such vehicles on public highways and principal thoroughfares. Senator Aquilino C. Pimentel, Jra, the principal author and sponsor of the bill that eventually has become to be known as the Local Government Code, has aptly remarked: Tricycles are a popular means of transportation, specially in the countryside. They are, unfortunately, being allowed to drive along highways and principal thoroughfares where they pose hazards to their passengers arising from potential collisions with buses, cars and jeepneys. The operation of tricycles within a municipality may be regulated by the Sangguniang Bayan. In this connection, the Sangguniang concerned would do well to consider prohibiting the operation of tricycles along or across highways invite collisions with faster and bigger vehicles and impede the flow of traffic.æ The need for ensuring public safety and convenience to commuters and pedestrians alike is paramount It might be well, indeed, for public officials concemed to pay heed to a number of provisions in our laws that can warrant in appropriate cases an incurrence of criminal and civil liabilities. Thus — The Revised Penal Code — The penalty of prision Art. 208. Prosecution of offenses; negligence and tolerance, correccional in its minimum period and suspension shall be imposed upon any public officer, or officer of the law, who, in dereliction of the duties of his office, shall maliciously refrain from instituting prosecution for the punishment of violators of the law, or shall tolerate the commission of offenses. The Civil Code — Ait. 27. Any person suffering material or moral loss because a public servant or employee refuses or neglects, without just cause, to perform his official duty may file an action for damages and other relief against the latter, without prejudice to any disciplinary administrative action that may be taken. 1 åwphil .nét Art. 34. When a member of a city or municipal police force refuses or fails to render aid or protection to any person in case of danger to life or property, such peace officer shall be primarily liable for damages, and the city or municipality shall be subsidiarily responsible therefor. The civil action herein recognized shall be independent of any criminal proceedings, and a preponderance of evidence shall suffice to support such action.

Ait. 2189. Provinces, cities and municipalities shall be liable for damages for the death of, or injuries suffered by, any person by reason of the defective condition of roads, streets, bridges, public buildings, and other public works under their control or supemsion. The Local Govemment Code — Sec. 24. Liability for Damages. — Local govemment units and their officials are not exempt from liability for death or injury to persons or damage to property. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, AT Y. JES S B. Dir ctor 11 r LS,08: OQUE IV
